Definition: 3rd person singular active present of G1210; also δέον; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding):--behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should.
BiblicalUsage: The little word means it must be, it is necessary, and the New Testament uses it wherever God's purpose presses on a life. Jesus says He must go to Jerusalem and suffer, a man must be born again, and the Son of man must be lifted up. The form itself is the impersonal of the verb to bind, and the manuscripts carry it under that verb's heading.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is the hinge of the gospel: what must be, God does, and what God must do, He does through Christ, because necessity in Scripture is never fate but the Father's purpose, and it always ends in redemption.
